messages.subject: Inflated abundance using distsamp
parts:
Hi folks,

I'm attempting to estimate abundance of birds on an Island from point counts using unmarked

Sites = 298
truncated distances = 0,5,10,15,20,25 m
Have followed the methods described in Kery et al 2016
the basic code I've used, at its simplest, follows

robin.umf <- unmarkedFrameDS(y=as.matrix(robin[,5:9]), siteCovs = data.frame(covs, area), dist.breaks=c(0,5,10,15,20,25), unitsIn = 'm', survey = 'point')
rob.N.hn <- distsamp(~1 ~1, robin.umf)
summary(rob.N.hn)

Call:
distsamp(formula = ~1 ~ 1, data = robin.umf)

Density:
 Estimate    SE    z  P(>|z|)
     1.52 0.178 8.52 1.55e-17

Detection:
 Estimate     SE    z  P(>|z|)
     2.27 0.0778 29.2 3.6e-187

AIC: 632.0539 

predict(rob.N.hn, type = 'state')

 Predicted        SE    lower  upper
1    4.550132 0.8088523 3.211519 6.4467

The problem I'm having is that the predicted abundance of 4.5 is waaaay higher than I would have expected from the data and my experience of the system.
This is ~3 times higher than what we actually observed (1.32). I've added a histogram of the detection distances, it appears to follow a pretty typical distribution for distance sampling observations.
I attempted GoF following Kery and found some over-dispersion (1.5) and that SSE and chisq indicated poor fit.

I have attempted all key functions, adding several environmental covariates, and have tried the negative binomial distribution using gdistsamp. In all cases I am getting the same estimate of abundance. Though NB in gdistsamp passed GoF for two tests.

I have also attempted the same modelling approaches with different species from the same dataset.

Again, my estimates of abundance are 2.5 - 3 times greater than the raw data indicates. 

How can I improve model fit from here? Or is there something fundamentally wrong with my approach, hence the inflation across multiple species and multiple models??
Help plz

Will
